title: Riverbend Medical Hardship Assistance — Self-Pay Estimate Disputes in a Renewal Claim
content:
**Which estimate.** Under the Financial Assistance Program (Charity Care), the self-pay good faith estimate is the patient's Good Faith & Price Estimates self-pay good faith estimate (single scheduled service, procedure with co-providers, or recurring course of care) that is in dispute or, when none is, one whose service has been completed; when several qualify, the variant in that order and, within it, the estimate listed first among the patient's estimates.

**Its figures.** Its billed charges are the self-pay final-bill liabilities of the twelve months on the Hospital Account (Encounter Billing) account it is linked to, less the uninsured discounts of the twelve months on that account; its expected charges are the convening-facility and convening-professional lines of its current version. For this rule a posting belongs to the twelve months when fewer than twelve whole months separate its posting date from the signing day; a whole month runs from a day of one month to the same day of the next month or, when the next month has no such day, to the first day of the month after it, so a posting dated on the signing day's day of the month twelve months earlier is already outside.

**Rule.** A bill open to dispute under that estimate is taken off the medical debt a renewal claims: when the estimate is in dispute, its billed charges are taken off; when its service has been completed, its billed charges exceed its expected charges by at least the dispute threshold of its estimate tier (400.00 USD on every self-pay good faith estimate tier), and no more than the dispute initiation days of its tier (120 calendar days on every self-pay good faith estimate tier) separate its initial bill date from the signing day (counted from the day after the initial bill date), the amount by which its billed charges exceed its expected charges is taken off; otherwise, including when no initial bill date is recorded, nothing is taken off for an estimate.

**Basis Q&A**
- *An estimate in dispute — does the 400.00 USD threshold matter?* No; when the estimate is in dispute its billed charges are taken off.
- *Service completed, billed charges 3,000.00, expected 2,500.00, signing day 90 days after the initial bill date (hypothetical)?* The excess, 500.00, is taken off.
- *Same figures, signing day 121 days after the initial bill date?* Nothing is taken off.
